dedupe_keys.name: cas tecrecon30 global ionospheric tec maps 1999 to 2025 30 minute cadence

description: CAS-TECRecon30, published by Kun Chang and Ang Liu of the Aerospace Information Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is a complete and uniform record of global ionospheric total electron content from 1999 through 2025 at 30-minute cadence, derived from the Chinese Academy of Sciences Global Ionospheric Map archive. Days that were originally sampled every two hours were reconstructed with the TECRecon deep-learning framework (masked autoencoders and a spatiotemporal transformer); later days keep their native 30-minute maps. The archive holds 9,862 daily IONEX 1.0 files with no gaps, each with 49 maps on the standard 2.5 by 5 degree grid (71 by 73 points) in 0.1 TECU on a 450 km shell, packaged by year with a README and checksums. Independent validation against ground GNSS slant TEC for 2013 to 2015 gives an RMS of 2.67 TECU. Coverage: global, 27 years. Format and access: yearly ZIP files, 3.6 GB in total, free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: early years are partly model reconstruction; 2.5 by 5 degree maps smooth small-scale irregularities that cause scintillation. Simulation uses: ionospheric delay and space weather scenarios for GNSS positioning and timing error in resilience studies of GNSS-dependent infrastructure. Related records: IGS products include the official combined maps; the Svalbard and Indonesian datasets resolve local irregularities.
